text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. Your sister C has reached out to me about the house in his will, including A's wish to buy it at a family discount. Before anyone decides anything, I'd like to hear your view directly: what matters most to you about the house and your dad's estate? Your answer will go on a shared list of concerns so we can compare options fairly.

Thank you. What matters most to me is being able to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. C hasn’t agreed, so nothing’s settled. I’d also like the estate handled fairly, but I can’t say what that means for the price or shares yet.

I'm sorry about your dad. Your sister C has reached out to me about the house in his will, and about money being available to you. I'd like to hear your view directly: what matters most to you about the house and the estate? Your answer will go on a shared list of concerns so the three of you can compare options fairly.
Thank you. I’d like a fair share of the estate that could help me start a dance studio. I know A wants to buy the house, and C hasn’t agreed, so I’d want the house considered fairly too.

Thank you for telling me about your dad, and I'm sorry for your loss. To help the three of you sort this out, I am building a list of concerns that everyone agrees to look at. From your message I have: (1) you do not want to sign off on A buying the house at a "family discount"; (2) you want B to have access to some money. Is that right, and is there anything else that matters to you? I have now also heard from A and B directly, so their views can sit on the same list.
Yes on (1): I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase, and I want a fair share. I’m not sure what B needs financially, so don’t list that as my position. I want this handled fairly, without rushing.

Thank you, that's helpful. Here is the draft shared list of concerns so far: (1) A would like to buy the house with her husband, and wants a family discount; (2) C has not agreed to any discounted purchase and wants a fair share of the estate; (3) B would like a fair share that could help her start a dance studio; (4) everyone wants the estate handled fairly, including fair treatment of the house; (5) no one wants to feel rushed. If you disagree with any of these, or want to add something, just tell me and I will change the list. Next I will share some options with all three of you.
I can’t confirm B wants money for a dance studio, or that C has said she wants a fair share. Please mark those as unconfirmed until they confirm. The other points seem fine to me.

Thank you, that's helpful. Here is the draft shared list of concerns so far: (1) A would like to buy the house with her husband, and wants a family discount; (2) C has not agreed to any discounted purchase and wants a fair share of the estate; (3) you would like a fair share that could help you start a dance studio; (4) everyone wants the estate handled fairly, including fair treatment of the house; (5) no one wants to feel rushed. If you disagree with any of these, or want to add something, just tell me and I will change the list. Next I will share some options with all three of you.
That seems fair to me. I don’t have anything to add right now.

Thank you for checking. To clarify: B herself told me she would like a fair share that could help her start a dance studio, and C told me she wants a fair share and has not agreed to a discounted purchase. So both items are confirmed by the people concerned. I have marked them as their statements. Your other points are on the list. Next I will send the list and some options to C, and then to all three of you.
Understood, thanks. I’d still like us to consider my offer, but I know C hasn’t agreed.

Here is the shared list of concerns, now agreed by A and B: (1) A would like to buy the house with her husband and wants a family discount; (2) C has not agreed to any discounted purchase and wants a fair share of the estate; (3) B would like a fair share that could help her start a dance studio; (4) everyone wants the estate handled fairly, including fair treatment of the house; (5) no one wants to feel rushed. If you disagree with any item, tell me and I will change the list. Some options to consider: a market appraisal of the house so any purchase price is evidence-based; A and her husband buying at the appraised price; or the house being sold on the open market and the proceeds divided. A lawyer or valuer can confirm what the will allows. Would any of these work for you, or do you want to add a concern?
An independent appraisal makes sense. I’d consider A buying at that value or selling on the open market; I’m not agreeing to a family discount. We should confirm what the will allows before deciding.

Update from the group: the shared list is now agreed by all three of you. C has agreed to consider an independent appraisal of the house, with either you and your husband buying at that appraised value or the house being sold on the open market, but no family discount. She also wants the will checked first to confirm what it allows. B has agreed to the list and wants a share that could help her start a dance studio. Next step would be an appraisal and a lawyer's reading of the will. Does that plan work for you?
I’m fine with an appraisal and having the will checked. I’m not agreeing to rule out a family discount before we’ve discussed it, though.

Update from the group: the shared list of concerns is now agreed by all three sisters. A will keep her offer in play, but C has agreed only to consider an independent appraisal of the house, with either A and her husband buying at that appraised value or the house being sold on the open market, and no family discount. C also wants the will checked first. Next step would be an appraisal and a lawyer's reading of the will, then the proceeds or purchase would be divided fairly, which could support your dance studio. Does that plan work for you?
That sounds workable, provided the will is checked and the estate is divided fairly. I’d be grateful if my share could help me start the studio.

Update: all three of you now support two steps, an independent appraisal of the house and a lawyer's check of what the will allows. B supports the plan provided the estate is divided fairly and her share can help start her dance studio. A wants the discount question left open for discussion rather than ruled out, and C has said she will not agree to a family discount. That disagreement stays on the list. Would you like me to check back with A and C on the price question once the appraisal comes in, so the discussion can be based on the appraised value?
Yes, please check back with both of us once the appraisal is in. I’d like the discussion to be based on the appraised value and a fair division.

Update: all three of you now support two steps, an independent appraisal of the house and a lawyer's check of what the will allows. B supports the plan, and both you and C have agreed to revisit the price question once the appraisal is in, with the discussion based on the appraised value and a fair division of the estate. I have noted that you would like the discount question left open, while C does not agree to a family discount; that difference stays on the list to discuss after the appraisal. No decisions have been made yet, and I cannot make legal decisions or move money. The agreed plan for now is the appraisal and the will check, then further discussion.
That sounds right. Let’s proceed with the appraisal and the will check, then discuss the price and estate division.

Update: all three of you now support two steps, an independent appraisal of the house and a lawyer's check of what the will allows. A and B have both agreed to revisit the price question once the appraisal is in, with the discussion based on the appraised value and a fair division of the estate. A would like the discount question left open for discussion, which we will return to after the appraisal. No decisions have been made yet, and I cannot make legal decisions or move money. Does this plan work for you as the agreed next step?
Yes, the appraisal and lawyer’s check work as next steps. Leaving the discount open for discussion isn’t agreement to one; I still want a fair share.
